meta.task: Create a versioned, cash-flow model and back-test it when verified inputs and comparable history exist; distinguish observations from assumptions
meta.version_policy: Any change to an assumption changes the version string. Observations do not bump the version unless the source vintage changes. This model is v0.1 because no property-level input exists yet; only the macro engine is built and tested.
meta.scope_honesty: The macro component below IS back-tested on real official data. The property-level cash-flow component is NOT, because it has zero verified inputs. Those two facts must never be presented together as 'a back-tested model'.

observations.statement: The Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim All-Transactions HPI rose from 282.59 (2015 Q1) to 553.76 (2026 Q3).
observations.note: 47 quarterly observations were extracted, 2015 Q1 through 2026 Q3.

observations.statement: That is a 6.03% compound annual growth rate over 11.50 years.
observations.note: Computed, not assumed. Arithmetic on OB-01.

observations.statement: Trailing 5-year appreciation in this metro has ranged from 4.57% to 9.04% per year across 27 rolling windows.
observations.unit: percent per year, min and max

observations.statement: The most recent trailing 5-year window (2021 Q3 to 2026 Q3) is 4.57% — the LOWEST in the entire sample.
observations.note: The boom of 2021-2022 has rolled out of the window. This is the single most useful fact for anyone tempted to underwrite continued 7% growth.

observations.statement: The metro index is 0.82% below its 2026 Q1 peak of 558.32.
The 10-year Treasury yielded 4.92% on 2026-11-23, after ranging 4.84% to 5.15% during November 2026.
Metro unemployment was 4.6% in October 2026, down from 5.3% in June 2026.
Local CPI rose 3.7% over 12 months to September 2026.
Only 4 earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or greater occurred in the central-LA bounding box in the 26 years from 2000 to 2026.

back_test.question: Does trailing appreciation predict forward appreciation in this metro?
back_test.design: Split the 47 quarterly observations into overlapping pairs: trailing 5-year CAGR versus the following 5-year CAGR. 7 usable pairs.
back_test.interpretation: Strongly NEGATIVE correlation. When the metro had been appreciating fast, the next five years were slower, and vice versa. Last five years 4.57%, next five whatever — extrapolation of the trailing rate is not merely unreliable here, it is systematically wrong in the same direction.
honest_limitations: Seven pairs is a very small sample. A 100% direction hit rate on seven observations is suggestive, not proof.
The index is metro-wide and weighted toward residential transactions. It cannot price a QSR pad and must not be used as the property's appreciation rate.
Overlapping windows are not independent, which overstates the apparent statistical strength.
The sample covers one interest-rate regime ending at 4.92% on the 10-year. A different rate regime could break the pattern.
back_test.conclusion: The macro engine passes its back-test for the purpose it is actually used for: refusing to extrapolate. It does not, and cannot, produce a property-level forecast.

assumptions.assumption: Base-case property appreciation is set to 0% real until property-level comps exist.
assumptions.justification: Back-test shows trailing rates are mean-reverting and the current trailing rate is already the sample low. Assuming zero real growth is the only defensible default. A reader can override it in the calculator and the override is theirs, not this model's.
assumptions.flip_risk: If central LA pads appreciate at even the sample-low 4.57% nominal, the hold case improves by roughly the cap rate differential each year. This is why the assumption is stated, not buried.

assumptions.assumption: Discount rate must be at least the 10-year Treasury plus a property risk premium the reader sets explicitly.
assumptions.justification: 4.92% is verified. The premium is not, so it has no default and the calculator will not run until the reader supplies one.

assumptions.assumption: Rent escalations are compared against local CPI of 3.7% rather than assumed to track it.
Property-level NOI, rent, expense recoveries, downtime, capex and renewal probability all remain UNSET.
assumptions.justification: Setting these without documents is the exact behaviour the owner prohibited. They are inputs in the browser calculator only.

cash_flow_engine.shape: Annual periods from the valuation date to a terminal year, with a separate terminal value block.

periods.contract_period: Valuation date to lease expiration. Rent is contractual; the only uncertainty is tenant default.
periods.option_period: Each renewal option, exercised or not, modelled as a probability-weighted branch rather than a single path.
periods.post_expiry_period: Vacancy, re-leasing cost, then market rent. This is where the hold case is usually weakest and where most simple models cheat by assuming instant re-lease at a higher rent.

cash_flow_engine.terminal_value: NOI at exit divided by an exit cap rate taken from a real quote (Q-01/Q-02). No exit cap rate is assumed here.
refusal_conditions: Exit cap rate missing → do not compute terminal value.
Discount rate missing → do not compute present value.
Lease expiration date missing → do not compute the contract period.
Insurance premium missing → compute, but stamp the output 'insurance unverified' because it is a top-three expense line.

scenario_skeletons.name: Renewal at market
scenario_skeletons.narrative: Tenant exercises its option; rent resets to market; no downtime.

scenario_skeletons.name: Tenant vacates at expiry
scenario_skeletons.narrative: Tenant leaves; 12-24 months of downtime; re-leasing cost; market rent thereafter.

scenario_skeletons.name: Sale now
scenario_skeletons.narrative: Sell at a quoted cap rate, net of selling costs, with the after-tax module applied.

scenario_skeletons.name: Sale now with §1031 deferral
scenario_skeletons.narrative: Same as SC-03 but gain deferred into a replacement property within 45/180 days.

governance.what_is_backtested: The macro engine: the mean-reversion test in this file, reproducible from the 47 official FHFA observations.
governance.what_is_not_backtested: Everything property-specific, because no property-specific data exists.
governance.next_version_trigger: v0.2 may be issued once lease dates, contract rent, an insurance premium and at least one real cap-rate quote are in hand. v0.2 must re-run this back-test and publish the error.
governance.rule: A model that cannot state its own error bars is a guess with a spreadsheet attached.
